results.evidence: Retry: the 1971 first-ascent report gives no grade; recent trip reports (May 2021, May 2026) and the Forest Service route page give no roman grade either; route pages that might carry one were not fetchable. The Forest Service says the route is best climbed early, before the glacier breaks up; dated ascents found are May 9 2026, May 30 2021 (via the ski-area lot) and the July 4-5 1971 first ascent, plus a February 2005 winter ascent. Sources lean to May-June but none states a window, and the Jun-Aug chip reflects when Artist Point is plowed; whether July is 'risky' is not stated by two sources. Would be settled by two sources giving an explicit climbing window.

results.fact: Which summit is the true high point
results.evidence: USGS point elevations along the summit ridge show three tops: about 7,165 ft at the route's summit pin (47.8258,-123.3340), about 7,177 ft near 47.8254,-123.3280 (the mountain's listed coordinate), and about 6,946 ft further east near -123.320; the two highest differ by less than DEM noise. A traverse report reaches the true summit first from Cameron Pass, then the Middle Peak, then the East Peak; a topo database titles the 7,190 ft point 'East Peak'. The names of the tops cannot be tied to the ground by two agreeing sources. Would be settled by a topo map or summit register naming which top is East/Middle.

results.correct_value: Upper Cameron Basin camp is open meadow/moraine near treeline, not old-growth forest.
results.evidence: A traverse report camped in upper Cameron Basin on a flat sandy spot beside the stream in glacial moraine with no tree cover. A separate backpacking report describes wildflower meadows fed by streams with camps in the middle of the basin, and a trail description says the trail clears treeline into a moonscape flat just below the pass. None describes old-growth forest at the camp.
